subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Halley's Comet
description: A fast breakdown of Halley's Comet for builders.

hook.text: Halley's Comet visits Earth every 75 years. Humans have recorded it for over 2,000 years.

buildup.text: Edmund Halley used Newton's gravity to predict its return in 1758. He was right but died before seeing it.

discovery.text: The tail forms when solar heat vaporizes surface ice. The solar wind pushes the gas away from the Sun.

twist.text: The Bayeux Tapestry shows Halley's Comet in 1066. Harold of England saw it before losing his throne.

climax.text: It last appeared in 1986. The next visit is 2061. Some alive today will see it twice.

punchline.text: One comet, millennia of wonder. Next visit: 2061.

quiz.question: How did Edmund Halley predict the comet's return?
options: He used Newton's laws of gravity to calculate its orbit
He found ancient records showing a regular pattern
He observed the comet moving in real time and projected its path

details.summary: Halley's Comet is the most famous periodic comet, returning to the inner solar system every 75-79 years. Edmund Halley predicted its return in 1758 using Newton's gravity — the first successful comet prediction.
details.whyItMatters: Halley's Comet proved that comets obey the same gravitational laws as planets — they're not unpredictable omens but regular visitors. Its orbital prediction was one of the first great triumphs of Newtonian physics.
takeaways: Halley's Comet returns every 75-79 years to the inner solar system
Halley predicted its 1758 return using Newton's gravity laws
The Giotto spacecraft imaged its nucleus during the 1986 pass

faq.question: When will Halley's Comet next be visible?
faq.answer: Halley's Comet will next reach perihelion (closest approach to the Sun) on July 28, 2061. It should be visible to the naked eye from Earth. Viewing conditions vary by approach — the 1986 apparition was unfavorable from Earth but provided the opportunity for the Giotto flyby.

faq.question: How far back have Halley's Comet appearances been traced?
faq.answer: Chinese records document its 240 BCE appearance, and it appears in the Bayeux Tapestry depicting the 1066 Norman conquest of England (Harold saw it as an omen). Calculations trace it back over 2,000 years. Its appearance has been linked to historical events across many cultures.
